goal_name: Ensure system and application access control

subgoals.objective_name: To prevent unauthorized access to systems and applications.
subgoals.goal_name: Prevent unauthorized access to systems and applications

subgoals.control_name: Access to information and application system functions shall be restricted in accordance with the access control policy.

subgoals.goal_name: Restrict access to information and application system functions in accordance with the access control policy
subgoals.embedding_context: Restrict access to information and application system functions in accordance with the access control policy

actions.name: System Call Filtering
actions.description: Controlling access to local computer system resources with kernel-level capabilities.

actions.name: Access Modeling
actions.description: Access modeling captures and records the access permissions granted to identities (e.g., administrators, users, groups, systems) and optionally includes details on how these identities are stored, managed, and shared across systems.

actions.name: Access Mediation
actions.description: Access mediation is the process of granting or denying specific requests to: 1) obtain and use information and related information processing services; and 2) enter specific physical facilities (e.g., Federal buildings, military establishments, border crossing entrances). Access mediation decisions should enforce least privilege by granting access for scoped durations to prevent privilege creep and, where applicable, implement just-in-time (JIT) access. Denial decisions may prevent initial access or terminate access that has already been granted, ensuring continuous enforcement of security policies.

actions.name: Access Policy Administration
actions.description: Access policy administration is the systematic process of defining, implementing, and managing access control policies that dictate user permissions to resources.

actions.name: Network Resource Access Mediation
actions.description: Control of access to organizational systems and services by users or processes over a network.

actions.name: Permissions Control
actions.description: Limit permissions to the minimum required.

actions.name: Privilege Control
actions.description: Limit LLM access and apply role-based permissions.

actions.name: Data Access Control
actions.description: Limit external data source access.

actions.name: Principle of least privilege
actions.description: Implement robust access control mechanisms, enforce the principle of least privilege, and regularly update and patch systems to close security gaps that could be exploited for privilege escalation.

actions.name: Network Restrictions
actions.description: Limit LLM access to resources and APIs.

subgoals.control_name: Password management systems shall be interactive and shall ensure quality passwords.

subgoals.goal_name: Ensure password management systems are interactive and shall ensure quality passwords
subgoals.embedding_context: Ensure password management systems are interactive and shall ensure quality passwords

actions.name: Strong Password Policy
actions.description: Modifying system configuration to increase password strength.

actions.name: Password Authentication
actions.description: Password authentication is a security mechanism used to verify the identity of a user or entity attempting to access a system or resource by requiring the input of a secret string of characters, known as a password, that is associated with the user or entity.

actions.name: Password Rotation
actions.description: Password rotation is a security policy that mandates the periodic change of user account passwords to mitigate the risk of unauthorized access due to compromised credentials.

actions.name: Restrict Library Loading
actions.description:
Prevent abuse of library loading mechanisms in the operating system and software to load untrusted code by configuring appropriate library loading mechanisms and investigating potential vulnerable software.
File formats such as pickle files that are commonly used to store machine learning models can contain exploits that allow for loading of malicious libraries.

actions.name: Trusted Library
actions.description: A trusted library is a collection of pre-verified and secure code modules or components that are used within software applications to perform specific functions. These libraries are considered reliable and have been vetted for security vulnerabilities, ensuring they do not introduce risks into the application.
